annotations.description: In Legacy, the vast majority of decks want to be on the play to have the tempo advantage of going first — playing a land first, casting the first spell, and having priority. Choosing to be on the draw is unusual and generally suboptimal unless you have a specific reason (e.g., a dedicated control or combo deck that values the extra card). Without knowing the exact deck, choosing to go second is a questionable decision since most competitive Legacy strategies benefit from going first.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to be on the draw (let Sonnet Tactic go first)
annotations.betterLine: Choose to be on the play (select yourself as starting player) to gain tempo advantage

annotations.description: Cast Personal Tutor before deploying Lion's Eye Diamond. In Legacy combo, the standard line is to play LED first (it's free at {0}), then cast Personal Tutor, allowing you to hold priority and crack LED in response to the tutor on the stack. This generates 3 mana while discarding the hand (which you're about to lose value from anyway since the tutor finds your key card). By casting Personal Tutor first without LED on the battlefield, they lose the option to crack LED in response.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Personal Tutor with Lion's Eye Diamond still in hand
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lion's Eye Diamond first (free), then cast Personal Tutor, retaining the option to crack LED in response to the tutor on the stack for 3 mana if needed

annotations.description: Casting Doomsday without a cantrip to immediately draw into the pile means passing the turn at 10 life with an empty hand, giving the opponent a full turn cycle to interact or develop their board. The opponent has 7 cards and a Goblin deck that could pressure quickly. Additionally, 3 useful cards (Polluted Delta, Edge of Autumn, Personal Tutor) are discarded to LED.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Doomsday using LED mana, discarding entire hand and going to 10 life with no immediate way to draw into the pile
annotations.betterLine: Wait for a turn where you have a cantrip available to immediately draw into the Doomsday pile after it resolves, or use Personal Tutor first to set up a better sequence. Playing the Polluted Delta from hand first would also preserve a land drop.

annotations.description: In a Doomsday pile execution, the player cast Ponder before playing their Polluted Delta as a land. Since cracking Lion's Eye Diamond in response to Ponder will discard the entire hand (including the unplayed Polluted Delta), the land drop is permanently lost. Playing Polluted Delta first preserves an additional fetchland on the battlefield, which could provide mana or deck manipulation during the combo turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ponder immediately without playing Polluted Delta as a land first.
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta as a land first, then cast Ponder (and crack LED in response to Ponder). This preserves the extra fetchland on the battlefield at zero cost.

annotations.description: Against a post-Doomsday opponent at 9 life with only 3 cards in library, KimiK2 chose Goblin Matron (1/1 without haste) over Broadside Bombardiers (2/2 with haste and menace). Bombardiers could attack immediately for 2, then use its Boast ability to sacrifice Aether Vial (which has done its job) to deal 2+1=3 damage to face, totaling 5 damage and putting the opponent to 4 life. Against a Doomsday pile, speed is critical as the opponent could combo off on their next turn. The tutor from Matron adds nothing urgent when KimiK2 already has strong cards in hand.

annotations.betterLine: Put Broadside Bombardiers onto the battlefield via Aether Vial, attack for 2 damage with haste+menace, then use Boast to sacrifice Aether Vial dealing 3 damage to face (total 5 damage, opponent to 4 life), maximizing pressure against the Doomsday pile.

annotations.description: Cast Brainstorm with only 2 cards remaining in library. Brainstorm requires drawing 3 cards, but the third draw from an empty library causes an immediate game loss via state-based actions. This is a post-Doomsday position where library size is critically important.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brainstorm with 2 cards in library, which attempts to draw 3 cards and results in drawing from an empty library (game loss).
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta as land drop first, then cast Personal Tutor (which shuffles library and puts a card on top, keeping library at 2+1=3 cards if there's a valid sorcery target), and only then cast Brainstorm safely. Alternatively, find a line that doesn't involve drawing more cards than exist in the library.
